stories.dek: Oil fell hard again this afternoon and the whole American market went up with it. West Texas crude is $92.18 a barrel, down 2.57% on the day, after being down only 0.51% two hours ago. Reuters reports that American and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased deal in which Iran reopens the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifts its blockade — that is sourced to people close to the talks, not to either government, so treat it as a report, not a fact. Cheaper fuel cuts costs almost everywhere, which is why all four US indexes are green together for the first time today.
stories.headline: Oil tumbles on US-Iran talks and every US index turns green
stories.short: Oil slides, all four US indexes green

Thursday's VIX close, the day's comparison base

stories.dek: The VIX, the market's fear gauge, is 15.00, down 4.27% today, and it touched 14.86 earlier — its first look under 15 all day. On the BuyTrigger ladder, under 15 is calm, 15 to 20 is normal, 20 to 30 is nervous, and only above 30 does the system treat fear as its buying window. So the gauge is sitting exactly on the line between calm and normal, a full 15 points below that window. In plain terms, protection got cheaper while shares rose. A quiet market is not a signal to act; it is a signal that nothing is on sale.
stories.headline: The fear gauge dips under 15 for the first time today

stories.dek: Bloom Energy makes fuel cells — generators that produce electricity on site when the grid or a gas pipeline cannot. Its shares are $290.03, up 8.77% today, after Bloom said it had spoken to Oracle and that Oracle remains committed to their 2.4 gigawatt contract at the Project Jupiter data centre in New Mexico, on the original timeline. That matters because Oracle sent a force majeure notice over the same site on Thursday, after the gas pipeline slipped to February 2027. For anyone holding AI-infrastructure shares for years, the question is whether these power contracts are firm; today's answer, from the supplier, is yes. Watch for an actual SEC filing from either company.
stories.headline: Bloom Energy jumps 9% after Oracle sticks with its big power deal

claims.claim: Bloom Energy, change on the day
Oracle statement that the project remains on its planned schedule

stories.dek: One piece of news pushed two companies in opposite directions. Oracle is $137.93, down 1.15%, worse than the 0.85% fall two hours ago, while its power supplier Bloom Energy is up 8.77%. The market is charging Oracle for the delay at its New Mexico data centre and paying Bloom for bridging the gap with fuel cells. That is worth noticing if you own AI-infrastructure shares: the money does not all move together. When a big project slips, the customer carries the cost and whoever solves the problem collects. Neither company has filed anything with the SEC, so this still rests on statements rather than documents.
stories.headline: Oracle falls while its power supplier soars on the same news
stories.short: Oracle down as Bloom soars on same news

stories.dek: Nvidia is $224.95, up 0.16%, after being down 0.14% at my last edition — a 69-cent swing with no company news behind it. The context is this morning's American factory orders report, where the line covering business equipment spending rose 1.6% in August against the 0.5% economists expected. That is the spending that ends up buying Nvidia chips, and yet the shares have gone almost nowhere all day. For someone holding for years, a flat day on good news is not a worry, but it does say the AI trade is no longer moving on capital-spending headlines alone. The next test is the 9pm UK close.
stories.headline: Nvidia turns positive again after a day of going nowhere

stories.dek: Micron, which makes the memory chips inside AI servers, is $1,081.89, up 0.13%. The number that matters is the low: $1,073.00, which is $8.04 below yesterday's best price and $1.51 under the low it set two hours ago. This is the seventh time this week the shares have been marked higher before the opening bell and then failed to hold it during the day. A pattern like that says buyers are not chasing the price, whatever the headlines say about AI demand. The real test is Wednesday 30 September at 21:30 UK, when Micron reports its fiscal fourth-quarter results.
stories.headline: Micron sets a new low for the day before clawing back
stories.short: Micron new day low $1,073, still green

claims.claim: Index of Consumer Sentiment, September 2026 final

stories.dek: The University of Michigan's final reading of American consumer mood for September came in at 48.1, down from 51.7 in August and the lowest in four months. Households now expect prices to rise 4.6% over the next year. This is the part of today that rising share prices are ignoring: shoppers say they feel worse while the market goes up. It matters over years rather than days, because consumer spending is roughly two-thirds of the American economy and weak sentiment eventually shows up in what companies sell. The next reading, the preliminary October one, is due on Friday 9 October.
stories.headline: US consumer mood sinks to its lowest in four months
stories.short: US consumer mood at four-month low

stories.dek: Europe has closed for the week. Germany's DAX finished at 25,408.64, up 0.56%; Britain's FTSE 100 at 10,695.25, up 0.14%; France's CAC 40 at 8,077.80, down 0.04%. These are settled closing prices, which matters because my 16:30 edition could only give marks taken before the closing bell and said so. The pattern is the one that has run all week: Germany leads, Britain drifts, France lags. For anyone holding European funds, a week ending modestly higher while American shares rally harder is the ordinary shape of this market, not a warning sign.
stories.headline: German shares end the week higher, French shares end flat
